radian.def: A unit of angle measure: an angle's radian measure is the length of the arc it cuts off divided by the radius. A full turn is $2\pi$ radians, so $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$. On the unit circle, an angle of $\theta$ radians cuts off an arc of length $\theta$.

unit-circle.def: The circle of radius 1 centered at the origin, $x^2 + y^2 = 1$. The terminal ray of an angle $\theta$ in standard position meets it at the point $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$.

standard-position.def: An angle placed with its vertex at the origin and its initial ray along the positive $x$-axis. It turns to its terminal ray, counterclockwise for a positive angle and clockwise for a negative one.

trig-function.def: The sine and cosine functions, and with them tangent, defined for any angle $\theta$ in standard position: $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ are the $x$- and $y$-coordinates of the point where the terminal ray meets the unit circle, and $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is the slope of the terminal ray.
